This made it write debug traces to plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log and trace-1.log at several MB/s, which took disk usage from 23 MB to about 119 MB within roughly a minute.
args.actions: 1) Saw disk usage grow from 23 MB to 42 MB in 30 s; fs_du showed the growth was plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log. 2) Declared an incident. 3) Read the AuditTrail config and logs and confirmed debug=true was reloaded at 06:38:40. 4) Edited plugins/AuditTrail/config.yml to set debug: false and left retention-days: 30 unchanged. The plugin hot-reloaded the config (log line "config reloaded (debug=false)" at 06:39:04). 5) Checked that disk usage stayed flat at 119 MB. 6) Deleted the runaway debug trace files trace-0.log and trace-1.log (about 93 MB of debug output, no player or audit data). 7) Watched for about 75 s: disk steady at 23 MB (5%), TPS 20, all plugins enabled, both players online. No restart, no bans. audit.log was not touched.
args.residual_risk: I don't know who or what turned debug on. If someone turns it back on, the disk will fill again because the debug traces have no size cap. The AuditTrail owner should be told and should add a size or rotation limit for debug output.
